chunks.text: # University Academic Regulations & Evaluation Guidelines (2025-2026)
chunks.citation: University Academic Regulations & Evaluation Guidelines (2025-2026) (General Overview)

chunks.text:
## 1. Credit Structure & Degree Requirements
1.1. The B.Tech degree requires the completion of a minimum of 160 academic credits across 8 semesters.
1.2. Each course is allocated a specific credit weighting based on lecture, tutorial, and practical contact hours (L:T:P).
1.3. A regular student must register for between 18 and 26 credits in any regular academic semester.
chunks.citation: University Academic Regulations & Evaluation Guidelines (2025-2026) (1. Credit Structure & Degree Requirements)

chunks.text: ## 2. Attendance Policy & Minimum Threshold 2.1. Every student is mandatorily required to maintain a minimum of 75% attendance in each registered course (lectures, tutorials, and laboratories independently). 2.2. Students with attendance between 65% and 74.9% may apply for Condonation of Attendance on valid medical grounds, supported by authenticated hospital documentation submitted within 7 days of discharge. 2.3. Condonation requires the approval of the Academic Council and payment of a statutory condonation fee of Rs. 1,000 per subject. 2.4. Students having attendance below 65% in any course will be detained from appearing in the Semester End Examination (SEE) for that specific course and awarded an 'NS' (Not Satisfied Attendance) grade. They must re-register for the course in a subsequent
chunks.citation: University Academic Regulations & Evaluation Guidelines (2025-2026) (2. Attendance Policy & Minimum Threshold)

chunks.text: Semester End Examination (SEE) for that specific course and awarded an 'NS' (Not Satisfied Attendance) grade. They must re-register for the course in a subsequent semester or summer term.
chunks.citation: University Academic Regulations & Evaluation Guidelines (2025-2026) (2. Attendance Policy & Minimum Threshold)

chunks.section_title: 3. Continuous Internal Evaluation (CIE) & Semester End Exams (SEE)
chunks.text:
## 3. Continuous Internal Evaluation (CIE) & Semester End Exams (SEE)
3.1. Total marks for each course: 100 Marks (50% CIE + 50% SEE weightage).
3.2. CIE components include two mid-term examinations (30 marks average), quizzes/assignments (10 marks), and course project/laboratory practicals (10 marks).
3.3. Minimum eligibility to appear for SEE: A student must secure a minimum of 40% (20 out of 50 marks) in the CIE component of the course.
chunks.citation: University Academic Regulations & Evaluation Guidelines (2025-2026) (3. Continuous Internal Evaluation (CIE) & Semester End Exams (SEE))

chunks.section_title: 4. Grading System & Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA)
chunks.text:
## 4. Grading System & Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA)
4.1. Letter grades and Grade Points:
- O (Outstanding): 90-100% -> 10.0 Grade Points
- A+ (Excellent): 80-89% -> 9.0 Grade Points
- A (Very Good): 70-79% -> 8.0 Grade Points
- B+ (Good): 60-69% -> 7.0 Grade Points
- B (Above Average): 55-59% -> 6.0 Grade Points
- C (Average): 50-54% -> 5.0 Grade Points
- P (Pass): 40-49% -> 4.0 Grade Points
- F (Fail): Below 40% -> 0.0 Grade Points

4.2. SGPA Formula: SGPA = Sum(Course Credit * Grade Points) / Sum(Total Semester Credits)
4.3. CGPA Formula: CGPA = Cumulative Sum(Course Credit * Grade Points) / Cumulative Sum(Total Registered Credits)
chunks.citation: University Academic Regulations & Evaluation Guidelines (2025-2026) (4. Grading System & Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA))

chunks.document_title: University Examination Ordinance & Hall Ticket Regulations
chunks.text: # University Examination Ordinance & Hall Ticket Regulations
chunks.citation: University Examination Ordinance & Hall Ticket Regulations (General Overview)

chunks.document_title: University Examination Ordinance & Hall Ticket Regulations
chunks.section_title: 1. Eligibility Criteria for Semester End Examinations (SEE)
chunks.text:
## 1. Eligibility Criteria for Semester End Examinations (SEE)
1.1. A student is eligible to receive a Digital Hall Ticket and sit for the Semester End Examinations only if:
- They satisfy the minimum 75% attendance criteria (or approved medical condonation) in the respective subject.
- They achieve at least 40% (20/50 marks) in Continuous Internal Evaluation (CIE).
- They have cleared all outstanding university tuition, hostel, and laboratory fee dues.
- No disciplinary action or exam debarment is pending against them.
chunks.citation: University Examination Ordinance & Hall Ticket Regulations (1. Eligibility Criteria for Semester End Examinations (SEE))

chunks.document_title: University Examination Ordinance & Hall Ticket Regulations
chunks.text:
## 2. Digital Hall Ticket & Cryptographic Verification
2.1. Eligible students must download their official Digital Hall Ticket from the ERP portal 7 days prior to the commencement of examinations.
2.2. The digital hall ticket contains a verifiable SHA-256 cryptographic QR code token containing student ID, seat allocation number, examination block, and approved subject codes.
2.3. Hall tickets must be presented to the Chief Superintendent or Invigilator alongside the physical university photo ID card for entry into the exam hall.
chunks.citation: University Examination Ordinance & Hall Ticket Regulations (2. Digital Hall Ticket & Cryptographic Verification)

chunks.document_title: University Examination Ordinance & Hall Ticket Regulations
chunks.text:
## 3. Examination Timetable & Seating Allocation
3.1. Morning session examinations are held from 09:30 AM to 12:30 PM.
3.2. Afternoon session examinations are held from 02:00 PM to 05:00 PM.
3.3. Students must report to their assigned examination room/hall at least 20 minutes prior to the scheduled examination start time. No candidate will be admitted 30 minutes after the commencement of the exam.
chunks.citation: University Examination Ordinance & Hall Ticket Regulations (3. Examination Timetable & Seating Allocation)

chunks.document_title: University Examination Ordinance & Hall Ticket Regulations
chunks.text:
## 4. Re-evaluation & Supplementary Makeup Examinations
4.1. Students may apply for photocopy of evaluated answer scripts within 5 working days of result declaration upon payment of Rs. 500 per paper.
4.2. Re-evaluation requests must be filed within 10 working days upon payment of Rs. 1,200 per paper. If marks improve by >= 15%, 50% of the re-evaluation fee is refunded.
4.3. Makeup / Supplementary examinations are conducted annually in July for students with backlogs or approved medical absentees.
chunks.citation: University Examination Ordinance & Hall Ticket Regulations (4. Re-evaluation & Supplementary Makeup Examinations)

chunks.document_title: University Fee Schedules, Hostel Guidelines & Financial Regulations
chunks.text: # University Fee Schedules, Hostel Guidelines & Financial Regulations
chunks.citation: University Fee Schedules, Hostel Guidelines & Financial Regulations (General Overview)

chunks.document_title: University Fee Schedules, Hostel Guidelines & Financial Regulations
chunks.section_title: 1. Tuition Fee Payment Schedules & Fine Slabs
chunks.text:
## 1. Tuition Fee Payment Schedules & Fine Slabs
1.1. Tuition and university academic fees for the odd semester must be paid on or before July 31st. Fees for the even semester must be paid on or before January 15th.
1.2. Late fee payment fine slabs:
- Up to 7 days post due date: Grace period (no late fine).
- 8 to 15 days delay: Rs. 500 fixed late fine.
- 16 to 30 days delay: Rs. 1,500 fixed late fine.
- Beyond 30 days delay: Rs. 3,000 late fine and temporary freeze of student portal access.
1.3. Fee receipts are digitally generated upon payment and can be downloaded from the Finance & Accounts section of the ERP.
chunks.citation: University Fee Schedules, Hostel Guidelines & Financial Regulations (1. Tuition Fee Payment Schedules & Fine Slabs)

chunks.document_title: University Fee Schedules, Hostel Guidelines & Financial Regulations
chunks.text:
## 2. Official Document Issuance & Verification Fees
2.1. Bonafide Certificate: Free of charge for first 3 copies per academic year; subsequent copies Rs. 100 each.
2.2. Official Grade Transcript / Consolidated Mark Sheet: Rs. 300 per semester copy.
2.3. No-Dues Clearance Certificate: Issued automatically upon clearance of all library, hostel, lab, and tuition accounts.
chunks.citation: University Fee Schedules, Hostel Guidelines & Financial Regulations (2. Official Document Issuance & Verification Fees)

chunks.document_title: University Fee Schedules, Hostel Guidelines & Financial Regulations
chunks.text:
## 3. Hostel Residency & Mess Regulations
3.1. Hostel room allotment is conducted at the beginning of each academic year based on merit and distance from hometown.
3.2. Hostel curfew hours: 09:30 PM for undergraduate students. Night-out permissions must be applied through the digital ERP at least 24 hours in advance and require automated OTP verification by registered parent/guardian.
3.3. Mess rebate policy: Students away from hostel for continuous periods exceeding 5 calendar days with approved leave are eligible for a 75% mess rebate credited to the subsequent month invoice.
chunks.citation: University Fee Schedules, Hostel Guidelines & Financial Regulations (3. Hostel Residency & Mess Regulations)

chunks.document_title: University Placement Policy & Campus Recruitment Norms (2025-2026)
chunks.text: # University Placement Policy & Campus Recruitment Norms (2025-2026)
chunks.citation: University Placement Policy & Campus Recruitment Norms (2025-2026) (General Overview)

chunks.document_title: University Placement Policy & Campus Recruitment Norms (2025-2026)
chunks.text:
## 1. Placement Registration & Eligibility Thresholds
1.1. All final-year and pre-final-year students registered with the Department of Corporate Relations & Placements are eligible to participate in on-campus recruitment drives.
1.2. Academic Thresholds:
- Tier-1 / Super Dream Companies (CTC > 20 LPA): Minimum CGPA of 8.00 or above, no active backlogs throughout the academic program.
- Dream Companies (CTC 10 LPA to 20 LPA): Minimum CGPA of 7.00 to 7.50, maximum 1 historical cleared backlog allowed.
- Core & Mass Recruiters (CTC up to 10 LPA): Minimum CGPA of 6.00 to 6.50, up to 2 historical cleared backlogs permitted.
chunks.citation: University Placement Policy & Campus Recruitment Norms (2025-2026) (1. Placement Registration & Eligibility Thresholds)

chunks.document_title: University Placement Policy & Campus Recruitment Norms (2025-2026)
chunks.section_title: 2. One Student - One Offer Policy (and Upgrade Rules)
chunks.text:
## 2. One Student - One Offer Policy (and Upgrade Rules)
2.1. Once a candidate secures an offer from a company with a package <= 10 LPA, they are considered 'Placed' and withdrawn from further drives with equivalent packages.
2.2. Dream Upgrade Rule: A student with an existing regular offer is permitted to interview for up to 3 Dream or Super Dream companies offering at least a 1.5x CTC increment over their existing offer.
2.3. Super Dream Upgrade: Any student securing an offer between 10 LPA and 20 LPA may appear for companies offering > 25 LPA.
2.4. Once an offer from a Super Dream company (> 20 LPA) is accepted, the candidate is strictly ineligible for further campus drives.
chunks.citation: University Placement Policy & Campus Recruitment Norms (2025-2026) (2. One Student - One Offer Policy (and Upgrade Rules))

chunks.document_title: University Placement Policy & Campus Recruitment Norms (2025-2026)
chunks.text:
## 3. Code of Conduct & Interview Protocol
3.1. Strict adherence to professional formal dress code is mandatory during pre-placement talks (PPTs), technical interviews, and HR discussions.
3.2. Failure to attend an interview round after being shortlisted without prior written approval from the Placement Officer will result in a 3-drive debarment penalty.
3.3. Dual acceptance of conflicting offers without placement cell consent will lead to immediate cancellation of all campus recruitment privileges and disciplinary notation.
chunks.citation: University Placement Policy & Campus Recruitment Norms (2025-2026) (3. Code of Conduct & Interview Protocol)
